title: Tour of the editor
summary: Where everything is, in five minutes. No experience needed.

steps.title: Welcome!
steps.say: Hi, I'm Dozer. This is the **editor**: the program we write code in. It has a lot of buttons, but you'll only use a few. I'll point at each part and say what it's for. Press **Next** to move along, whenever you're ready.

steps.title: The Explorer
steps.say: This list is the **Explorer**. It shows everything in your project: your **files** and **folders**. Think of it as the list of what's in your backpack.

steps.title: The icon bar
steps.say: These icons switch what the left panel shows. The top one is the Explorer (your files). The magnifying glass is **Search** (find words in all your files). The branching one is **Source Control** (saving versions of your work with git). You'll meet them later.

steps.title: Where files open
steps.say: This big area is where a file opens so you can read it and type in it. Every open file gets a **tab** at the top, just like tabs in a web browser. Click a tab to switch files; click the **x** on it to close it.

steps.title: The terminal
steps.say: Now let's open one more thing. Press **Ctrl+`** (the key just above Tab) to open the **terminal**. Click somewhere in the editor first, so it hears your keys.

steps.title: What the terminal is
steps.say: The terminal is a place where you give the computer instructions by **typing** instead of clicking. When you run a program, its words show up here too. We'll practice in a later guide.

steps.title: The status bar
steps.say: The thin bar at the very bottom is the **status bar**. It tells you little things: what kind of file is open, and a count of **problems** (mistakes the editor found in your code). Zeros are good.

steps.title: Scriptum's own bar
steps.say: Up at the top is Scriptum itself. This chip shows the lesson you're in. Open it to see your **checkpoints** (the little jobs to finish) and press **Verify** to check your work.

steps.title: That's the tour
steps.say: That's everything you need to get going. Come back to me any time: press the **Dozer** button at the top and pick a guide. Try **What are files and folders?** next.
